key_insight: ARGUS turns long, complex U.S. employment-discrimination complaints into structured Event Knowledge Graphs, making legal events and relationships easier for models to understand. Its role-aware, source-grounded pipeline goes beyond bag-of-words or embeddings by capturing who did what, when, and why.
problem_solved: Employment-discrimination complaints contain multi-step narratives with actors, timelines, and causal links that are hard to represent with standard lexical or embedding-based methods. The paper addresses the need for document-level structured representations that preserve legal facts from CourtListener complaints.
method: Uses a 5W1H-inspired schema to identify fact-bearing statements and key event attributes.
Combines legal-domain models with LLM-based structured generation to build chunk-level event graphs from complaint text.
Aggregates chunk-level graphs into document-level Event Knowledge Graphs with participant, temporal, and causal structure.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ARGUS shows how to build grounded, interpretable document representations for complex legal texts. This can improve downstream tasks such as retrieval, reasoning, case analysis, and information extraction in high-stakes domains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: complaint text -> fact extraction -> chunk-level event graph -> document-level EKG
5W1H schema wheel or grid showing who/what/when/where/why/how
Example event graph with nodes for people, events, and causal/timeline edges
Side-by-side comparison of raw complaint text vs. structured graph representation
paper_title: ARGUS: Role-Aware Event Knowledge Graphs for U.S. Employment-Discrimination Complaints
paper_authors: Sriram Kannan, Swetha Saseendran, Vishnu Vardhan Reddy Kandi, Leslie Barrett, Madhavan Seshadri
